summary.headline: MTAR Q1 FY27 revenue rose 130.4% YoY to INR360.7 crore with a 23.5% EBITDA margin; closing order book stated at INR5,143 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR360.7 crore, up 130.4% YoY from INR156.6 crore, with EBITDA of INR85.1 crore (23.54% margin) and PAT of INR50.2 crore. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 80% revenue growth and a 24% ±100 bps EBITDA margin, and said it expects to do better. Working capital days fell sharply to 59 from 172 days for FY26, and management said debt is near nil after investments. Management highlighted civil nuclear order inflows, fuel cell capacity expansion in three phases, and a new data centre infrastructure product line.

segments.name: Civil nuclear
segments.commentary: Highest-ever order inflow in the quarter for Kaiga 5 & 6; current nuclear order book about INR684 crore, with INR130-140 crore refurbishment orders expected in Q1 FY28 and about INR800 crore total nuclear book targeted. Execution of Kaiga 5 & 6 runs 1-3.5 years; refurbishment orders within 2 years; ramp-up starts H2 FY27.

segments.name: Clean Energy (fuel cells)
segments.commentary: Record order inflows in the quarter. Phase 1 capacity commissioned; Phase 2 due Sept-Oct 2026; Phase 3 (multifold expansion) due March 2027. Data centre infrastructure products entered; first batch of about INR45 crore for export due by March 2027.

segments.name: Aerospace and defence
segments.commentary: Management expects to double aerospace and defence revenue in FY27, with a 3-4 year ramp. Domestic defence opportunity above INR250 crore, including Tejas Mk-1A actuator assemblies (about INR140-150 crore program value). Oil & gas facility operational by October 2026.

segments.name: Products and others
segments.commentary: Revenue jumped to about INR100 crore in the quarter, roughly 50% of the Clean Energy run-rate per the analyst's framing; management says it will keep growing and H2 will be stronger than H1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of about 80%, reiterated; management said it is confident of doing better.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 24% ±100 bps; Q1 margin of 23.54% described as in line.
Closing order book target of about INR5,000 crore by FY27 end; Q1 closing book of INR5,143 crore plus about INR800 crore received after quarter end.
Working capital days target about 100 by FY27 end; ROCE target 23% next year.
Capex of about INR500 crore over FY27 and FY28 (70% Clean Energy, 30% other), with spillover into the next 1-2 quarters; asset turnover target 4-6x. FY28 guidance not given formally.
Aerospace and defence: FY30 potential cited at INR600-700 crore; products division potentially above INR1,000 crore.

financial_highlights.value: INR423.6 crore as of 30 June 2026; net debt about INR20-30 crore after investments of INR379 crore

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR3,100 crore of orders announced on the call be executed in FY28-FY29 rather than FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the newly announced orders are for next financial year and execution depends on how fast the expansion and ramp-up plans are implemented.

qa_highlights.question: What are the refurbishment order size and the execution timelines for the existing nuclear orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Refurbishment orders are about INR200 crore overall, with INR130-140 crore expected this quarter; refurbishment execution within 2 years, Kaiga 5 & 6 execution 1-3.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will fuel cell capacity go beyond the guided 20,000 hot boxes, and what is the Phase 3 timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 operational by September-October 2026; Phase 3 is a multifold expansion commissioned by March 2027, with ramp-up from April; numbers not disclosed due to NDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the products revenue run-rate sustainable, and what is its scope beyond the fuel cell hot box?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will continue to grow, H2 will be stronger than H1, and it includes ball screws for export and an MNC aerospace contract, not only fuel cell assemblies.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivable and inventory days and the working capital target of about 100 days be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better commercial and credit terms with customers, daily/weekly monitoring, and GST refund of about INR70 crore per year; working capital at 59 days now, target below 100 days for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex was spent in Q1 and what is the FY27-28 capex split and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR30-35 crore spent in Q1 (INR80 crore capitalised from CWIP); INR500 crore total over FY27-28 with 70:30 Clean Energy to other split; funded by a combination of internal accruals and debt.

qa_highlights.question: Can management raise the FY27 revenue growth guidance given a key client's upward revision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated it expects to do better than 80% growth guidance but will revisit the outlook by end of next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Tejas and defence content per platform and the nuclear wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Tejas actuator program about INR140-150 crore; management said other defence niche projects are in progress and nuclear wallet share is 60-70% for NPCIL/DAE reactors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the interest cost breakdown and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the break-up on the call and said interest cost would decline quarter-on-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are there delays at US data centre customers' capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees no issue and that the reports are unwanted noise, with orders moving in the right direction.

capex_capacity: Capex of about INR500 crore across FY27 and FY28 for existing expansion plans; management said spend will spill over 1-2 quarters into next financial year, with a 70:30 split between Clean Energy and other segments.
Capex incurred in Q1 FY27 about INR30-35 crore; INR80 crore moved from capital WIP to fixed assets during the quarter.

Fuel cell capacity in three phases: Phase 1 commissioned, Phase 2 due September-October 2026, Phase 3 multifold expansion due commissioning by March 2027 (ramp-up from April 2027). Specific capacity numbers withheld under NDA.
Oil & gas facility to be operational by October 2026; first articles already delivered to one customer, first articles for another in progress.

Dedicated facility being set up for data centre infrastructure solutions; aerospace sub-units being added within existing dedicated aerospace facility; NADCAP-approved special processes facility in place.
Asset turnover target at least 4-6x (management cited 4-5x and then at least 6x); next-year capex guidance not given formally.
demand_pricing: Closing order book INR5,143 crore at 30 June 2026; management said about INR800 crore of further orders were received on the call date, taking the book to about INR5,900 crore (analyst cited INR3,100-3,200 crore incremental figure, management clarified incremental INR800 crore).

Civil nuclear: current order book about INR684 crore; INR130-140 crore refurbishment orders expected in the current quarter; total nuclear book about INR800-815 crore, to be executed over about 3 years; execution to start in H2 FY27. Highest-ever nuclear order inflow in Q1 for Kaiga 5 & 6.

Clean Energy: record order inflows in Q1; data centre infrastructure first batch about INR45 crore, all for export, to be executed by March 2027; management sees potential requirement of 8 such sets per year.

Products and others revenue about INR100 crore in Q1, which management said will keep growing with H2 stronger than H1; drivers include ball screws (export orders and a major MNC contract for aerospace) and other qualified products.

Aerospace and defence: management expects revenue to double in FY27; domestic defence opportunity above INR250 crore including Tejas Mk-1A actuator assemblies (program value about INR140-150 crore); MNC aerospace volume ramp-up from qualified products.
Management said the order book is largely short-cycle (within 2 months to 2 years, mostly under 1 year) and that execution of recent orders is largely next fiscal year.

Mahi Banswara: four 700 MW reactors via NTPC-NPCIL, tenders floated; management expects orders in the next financial year and says MTAR's share could exceed Kaiga 5 & 6 (two reactors), with participation through EPC vendors.
Gross margin 45.61% vs 47.65% a year ago, attributed to revenue mix; management expects product mix and operating leverage to support margins.
risks_watch: Execution risk: management says most new orders execute in FY28-29 and depends on Phase 2 and Phase 3 capacity commissioning timelines (Oct 2026 and March 2027).

Working capital: target of about 100 days by FY27 end versus 59 days in Q1; sustainability of receivable and inventory day reductions is unproven, and management said some improvements came from negotiated terms.
Margin: Q1 gross margin fell to 45.61% from 47.65%; EBITDA margin 23.54% is below the 24% guidance midpoint; product mix may dilute margins.
Funding: INR500 crore capex plus working capital to be funded through internal accruals and debt; net debt of about INR20-30 crore after investments may change.

Concentration and disclosure: heavy reliance on a single key client for fuel cell and data centre orders, with capacity numbers and data centre volumes withheld under NDA; US data centre capex slowdown was raised by an analyst and dismissed by management.
key_quotes: We expect to double our revenues in aerospace and defense segment during the current fiscal year, with a significant ramp-up from this base and spread over the next 3 to 4 years.
Our closing order book by end of this quarter already stands at INR5,143 crores, and we have received additional INR800 crores of orders today.
So, the best part of our order book, it's not like an order book which has to be executed over 5 years or 10 years, it's all short cycle.
Phase 2 to be commissioned by September-October of this year, while Phase 3, which is a multifold capacity expansion, will be completed in March of 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-leaning on demand, order book and guidance (said it expects to do better than 80% revenue growth), but guarded and non-specific on capacity numbers, nuclear tender timelines and interest cost, citing NDA and unavailable data. Several answers were long and repetitive, with the CFO giving more precise figures than the MD.
